name: Albany International Airport
before:
The air centre for the Capital Region, north eastern New York and western New England, six miles north west of Albany. It is the fourth largest airport in the state.

Traffic reached a record in 2025 at just under 1.6 million departing passengers, finally passing the previous high set back in 2004.

The airline mix is the useful part for pricing. Southwest holds around a third of the traffic on its own, and JetBlue, Allegiant and Avelo all serve the airport too, so this is a low cost heavy market and fares tend to reflect that.

It sits close to Interstate 87 and state routes 155 and 7, which makes onward driving into the Adirondacks or across to New England straightforward.

The site covers 1,000 acres in the town of Colonie, built on land that was once a Shaker settlement, and is owned by the Albany County Airport Authority.
after:
The air centre for the Capital Region, north eastern New York and western New England, about seven miles north west of Albany. It is the fourth largest airport in the state.

Traffic reached a record in 2025 at just under 1.6 million departing passengers, finally passing the previous high set back in 2004.

The airline mix is the useful part for pricing. Southwest holds around a third of the traffic on its own, and JetBlue, Allegiant and Avelo all serve the airport too, so this is a low cost heavy market.

It sits close to Interstate 87, which makes onward driving into the Adirondacks or across to New England straightforward.

The airport is run by the Albany County Airport Authority, which leases it from Albany County. It lies in the town of Colonie, on land that was once part of a Shaker settlement.

claims.note: Was 'is owned by the Albany County Airport Authority'. The Authority's own annual report says the County leases the airport to it (lease now running to 31 December 2049) and NYSDOT's directory calls the Authority the lessee of the owner, Albany County; Wikipedia's lead says the Authority owns it, but its infobox and history say the county owns it and leases it. The FAA's master record lists the Authority as owner; the report says the FAA approved the transfer of the airport's sponsorship from the county to the Authority in 1996, which would account for that.
